ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the main circuit of a three-phase motor. In the upper left there is a three-phase power supply L1, L2, L3, which enters three main circuits through the QS switch; in the lines there are the FU1 fuse and the three-phase contacts of the main contactor KM1; in the three-phase stator lines leading to the motor M (3~), resistors labeled R are connected in series; on the right side, the contacts of KM2 are connected in parallel with these resistors, used to bypass the resistors during operation; at the bottom there are also the thermal relay FR and the three-phase motor terminals U, V, W. Reasoning: During motor starting, the main circuit connects resistors in series into the stator winding circuit to reduce the voltage applied to the stator, and after starting is completed, the KM2 contacts short-circuit the resistors to enter normal operation. Therefore, this main circuit belongs to a stator-winding series-resistor reduced-voltage starting control circuit.

method.method_draft: First describe the image structure: identify the three-phase source, main contactor KM1, the motor M, the resistors R in each stator phase line, and KM2 contacts that bypass the resistors. Then use the text question, which asks what type of control circuit this main circuit belongs to. Apply the motor-control rule that a main circuit with series resistances in the stator circuit during starting and a bypass contactor for normal running is a stator winding series resistance step-down starting control circuit. Return that name.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct component-topology identification: it classifies the circuit by recognizing the series resistors and their bypass contactor in the motor stator supply path.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram as a three-phase motor main circuit: L1/L2/L3 feed through QS, FU1 and KM1 to the motor M 3~ via terminals U/V/W; three resistors marked R are placed in series in the three stator phase lines before the motor; contactor KM2 has contacts wired in parallel with those resistors to short/bypass them after starting; FR is the overload relay.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt only to know that the required output is the type/name of the control circuit shown by the main circuit.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: In three-phase motor starters, adding resistors in series with the stator windings during startup lowers the applied stator voltage and starting current; a later contactor bypass of those resistors identifies a stator-resistance reduced-voltage, or step-down, starting circuit.
